rfm_tuples.R: Implied by mgmt narrative: 'As the adoption of our platform and solutions accelerates, we expect to strengthen customer relationships, enhance recurring revenue streams and broaden monetization opportunities' (10-K MD&A) — i.e. mgmt is confident in turnaround at depressed share price.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B implied-verification: if the new CEO and executive officers truly believed the platform-transition thesis at the all-time-low share price post -55% drawdown, expect open-market Form 4 code-P purchases by C-suite into the drawdown.
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO open-market purchases (code P) by ANY officer or director in the 12 months preceding cutoff (2025-05-26 → 2026-05-13). All 25 reviewed Form 4 transactions are: code A (director equity-comp grants 2025-06-06), code M (RSU vest/exercise), code F (sell-to-cover tax withholding at $6.50–$13.18), code G (CEO Kelly GIFTED 113,753 shares on 2026-05-12, 13 days before cutoff). Directors received cashless RSU grants on 2025-06-06; none subsequently purchased. CFO Webb-Walsh, GC Sterrett, Pres Restaurants Tadele, Pres Retail Wilson, CAO Wise all received March-2026 RSU grants and sold-to-cover (code F at $6.50–$8.01) — they only NETTED shares from RSU vests, none ADDED via open market.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B Form-4 contradiction: in a -55% drawdown, with the company simultaneously buying back $74M of its own common stock (May-Dec 2025) and authorizing another $178M repurchase Feb 2026, NOT ONE insider has used personal capital to buy a single open-market share. New CEO James Kelly (appointed Feb 4, 2025) has had 15 months in seat and gifted away shares rather than buy. This is the classic asymmetric pattern: company spends shareholder cash defending the price; insiders quietly extract via RSU vest+sell-to-cover and gift. Form 4 evidence directly contradicts the management 'confidence in platform-led recovery' narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied by CEO compensation framing: large March-2026 RSU grants (87,022 + 620,066 RSUs) signal long-term commitment.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B Form-4 + insider_vs_calendar: examine CEO Kelly's personal share economics relative to Q1 2026 earnings (10-Q filed 2026-05-07) and stock-price action.
rfm_tuples.M_value: On 2026-05-12, six days after the May-7 Q1 10-Q release, CEO Kelly transferred 113,753 shares (his entire common-stock position, equal to all shares received from March 3+15 RSU vests) via code G (gift). Post-transaction holding: ZERO direct common shares. This is the FIRST gift by the CEO post-appointment and occurred 13 days before our cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Code-G gifts are not typically alpha-bearing, BUT timing is striking: CEO divests his entire common holding via gift immediately after Q1 earnings and shortly before cutoff. Combined with the absence of any open-market buy, this is the strongest possible negative-asymmetric Form-4 signal. The 620,066-share market-based RSU grant suggests Kelly views his entire upside as gift-able paper, not personally-purchased equity.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'Revenue was $2.7 billion, decreased 5% compared to prior year' with framing that '[r]ecurring revenue increased 3%' and 'Adjusted EBITDA of $425 million, increased 22%'.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A check the GAAP top line and Mode-B verify recurring-mix improvement is organic vs definitional/divestiture-driven.
rfm_tuples.M_value: GAAP revenue: 2025 $2,687M / 2024 $2,818M / 2023 $3,166M — a 15% decline over two years. Hardware revenue: 2025 $701M / 2023 $1,058M (-34% two-yr). 'Recurring revenue' grew because the denominator collapsed (hardware divested to Ennoconn ODM, beginning April 2026 booked as net commission), not because actual recurring $ accelerated. Operating income $26M on $2,687M revenue = 1.0% operating margin.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'recurring revenue mix improved' narrative is an arithmetic artifact of divesting hardware. Actual recurring revenue grew only 3% ($1,629M → $1,676M) — single-digit organic growth for a company telling investors it's a 'platform-powered leader in unified commerce'. The 22% Adj EBITDA growth is largely tax-benefit + cost-cut driven (transformation costs still $124M).

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'On February 12, 2026, the Board amended the Repurchase Program to add an incremental $178 million of repurchase authority… taking the total aggregate repurchase authority… to $300 million' — capital allocation framed as opportunistic.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: who is buying the company's stock right now? Compare issuer buyback ($74M common + $74M preferred in 2025; new $178M authority Feb-2026) vs insider open-market purchases ($0).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Company repurchased $74M common in 2025 (~6.5M shares at ~$11 avg) and $74M preferred. Q1 2026: another $9M common repurchased. Aggregate ~$157M company spend on its own shares in the 17 months preceding cutoff. Insiders' personal open-market spend on VYX shares over same window: $0.00.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic 'company buying, insiders not buying' divergence. Mgmt is happy to deploy $157M of shareholder cash supporting the share price while personally only extracting (RSU sell-to-cover + CEO gift). This is the cleanest single-name example of the honesty-alpha framework's negative-asymmetric signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'At December 31, 2025, we had approximately $1.1 billion of total indebtedness outstanding with an additional $476 million of borrowings available under our senior secured revolving credit facility' — framed as ample liquidity.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A verify leverage ratio cushion vs the 4.25x covenant; Mode-B check whether the buyback drains liquidity into the covenant headroom.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total debt $1.1B; consolidated leverage covenant capped at 4.25x EBITDA (was 4.50x prior to Q3 2025). 2025 Adj EBITDA $425M ⇒ ratio ~2.6x — passing today. But cash $232M (Q1 2026) down from $758M at Dec 2024, after $2.45B Digital Banking sale proceeds. Issuer simultaneously committing $300M to buybacks AND running operating losses ($19M Q1 op loss).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Covenant headroom looks fine on the trailing measure, but the company has burned through $500M+ of cash in 12 months while authorizing aggressive buybacks. Q1 2026 op loss + ongoing transformation costs + Kalamazoo environmental reserve build = compounding draws on the cushion. Not imminent distress, but mgmt is using shareholder cash to defend a stock the insiders won't personally back.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Adj EBITDA add-back schedule and 10-Q: 'transformation and restructuring costs… considered non-operational in nature' — $124M (2025), $125M (2024), with another $23M in Q1 2026.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: are these costs recurring year-after-year? Mode-B: if they keep occurring, the 'non-recurring' framing of the Adj EBITDA bridge is a narrative violation.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Transformation/restructuring add-backs: 2023 $28M, 2024 $125M, 2025 $124M, 2026 Q1 $23M annualized $92M. Strategic-initiative add-backs: 2024 $48M, 2025 $16M, 2026 Q1 $18M (annualized $72M). 'Special items' are now $200M+/yr for three consecutive years.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Items labeled 'non-operational' have run >$200M every year since 2024. Reported Adj EBITDA of $425M overstates the underlying run-rate by ~$200M of recurring 'one-time' charges. GAAP op income was only $26M for FY2025. The 22% Adj-EBITDA-growth headline relies on classifications mgmt itself has shown to be permanent.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'In April 2023…cyber ransomware incident…cumulative $47M of expenses…recovered $37M' and 'In February 2024…fraudulent ACH disbursements…cumulative $34M…recovered $16M'.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: confirm net loss exposure; Mode-B: is this 'fully remediated' control story credible given recurrence?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cyber: $47M gross / $37M recovered ⇒ $10M net loss; insurance cap unclear. ACH fraud: $34M gross / $16M recovered ⇒ $18M net loss outstanding, with insurance recovery uncertain ('there can be no assurance'). 10-K Item 9A says 'material weaknesses…fully remediated in fiscal 2024' but ACH fraud occurred Feb 2024 — i.e. during the very period of supposed remediation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two separate ~$30-40M control-failure incidents (cyber 2023, internal-ACH 2024) at a company that says material weaknesses are 'fully remediated'. Mode-B: the ACH fraud is an unforced internal-control failure that occurred during the very fiscal period management says controls were fixed. Net exposure ~$28M is non-fatal but the pattern dents credibility on the 'we have it under control' frame.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'During the third quarter of 2025, the Company identified errors in previously issued financial statements related to the historical pre-Spin-Off operations of NCR Atleos… concluded that they were immaterial… However, the Company is revising the previously issued financial statements'.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A check whether the revision is truly immaterial; Mode-B check whether 'identified in Q3 2025' aligns with the steep share-price drawdown.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revision reduces previously reported NI from discontinued ops by $5M (2023) and $6M (2022). Decreases opening retained-earnings (deficit) by $8M at 12/31/2022. Plus separate out-of-period adjustments: $10M revenue cut (Q2 2024, of which $4M pre-2024), $8M FX (Q3 2024, of which $2M from 2023). 'Immaterial individually and in aggregate'.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Revisions are small ($5-10M) and isolated to discontinued/out-of-period items but represent the THIRD consecutive year of out-of-period accounting corrections (2023 Q1, 2024 Q2, 2024 Q3, 2025 Q3) at a company whose prior material-weakness narrative is supposedly 'fully remediated'. Pattern matters more than amount.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: '[A]s a result of the Hardware Business Transition, we will record commission revenue from point-of-sale and self-checkout hardware sales as an agent for Ennoconn on a net basis, excluding the costs paid to Ennoconn.… a substantial majority of the revenue related to the sale of hardware will no longer be recognized by us'.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A quantify the revenue step-down; Mode-B check whether mgmt has guided to the resulting reported revenue baseline.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Hardware revenue 2025: $701M (26% of total). 10-Q (filed May 2026) states 'beginning on April 1, 2026, the Company began recording commission revenue from point-of-sale and self-checkout hardware sales as an agent for Ennoconn on a net basis'. NO pro-forma revenue baseline disclosed for post-transition. NO 2026 full-year revenue guidance disclosed in either 10-K or 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: mgmt is engineering a ~$500M+ revenue optical drop (gross-to-net) starting Q2 2026 but has NOT given the market a clear post-transition baseline. Investors comparing 2026 reported revenue to 2025 will see a 20%+ headline decline that is purely accounting-driven — and the company has chosen not to publish a comparable bridge. This sets up an avoidable Q2/Q3 narrative disaster.
